title: Paris Fashion Week: A report from the ground | CNN
text:
EDITOR’S NOTE:CNN Style is one of the official media partners ofParis Fashion Week. See all coveragehere.

Source: CNN

Paris Fashion Week, the biggest arena for the industry’s battle of ideas, has wrapped after nine days of shows.Rihanna was spotted, and maniacal crowds lined up outside shows to screech and wave at their favorite stars all week. Chanel, and designer Matthieu Blazy,made everyone hungry for more, proving the brand’s winning streak is not over.

If Monday’s opening day was defined by a series of thinky shows by emerging ingenues including the creative duo behind Matières Fécales, Swedish one-to-watch Ellen Hodakova Larsson, and LVMH prize-winner Julie Kegels, Tuesday was when big houses like Dior and Saint Laurent ramped things up with their high octane productions and masterful collections.

Cult brand Maison Margiela, the label behind the freaky looking tabi shoe, also staged its latest renegade runway show. Against a backdrop of wilting flowers that left a subtle funk in the air, designer Glenn Martens once again put forth ideas that challenged conventions of beautiful clothing. Models walked in toeless, knee-high boots in sculpted blazers and shirts that left the chest open and gaping, and floral prints clashed with the set behind them.

The inclined runway at Rick Owens, which begins at the top of the Palais de Tokyo and crosses over the fountain, always makes models look as if they are descending off the ramp of a spaceship that travelled here from another galaxy. That feeling was intensified on Thursday, as Owens sent down prismatic tentacle “dresses” where tulle trim was threaded onto elasticated cords that pinged around as models walked.

Olivia Coleman’s surprise runway cameo at Miu Miu was made even better by her new gray locks. And Michael Rider’s latest collection for Celine offered yet more ideas for looking effortlessly divine.

See all our highlights below as we zoom in and out on the little delights and big moments that grabbed our attention.

The typical photographer pit stationed at the end of a runway can’t quite capture the unexpected three-dimensional shape of Duran Lantik’s designs. For his Spring-Summer 2027 collection at Jean Paul Gaultier, Lantik brought out cone bras, of course, but also halter-neck straps that looped in front of a model’s collar bones like a rollercoaster track, or a bra connected to a pair of underpants via two bridges of fabric. One of the most intriguing pieces was a cropped ‘flannel’ shirt worn more like a bib, where the empty entrance hole was purely decorative.

Jean Paul Gaultier himself, who sat front row with a perfect side-on view, was pleased — hugging Lantik after the finale.

Miu Miu, Miuccia Prada’s more spritely fashion offering, has built a reputation not just for its unexpected remixes of girlish dress codes — but for facilitating a few runway surprises, too.

There was Miranda July for Spring-Summer 2023, Willem Dafoe for Spring-Summer 2025 and Sarah Paulson for Fall-Winter 2025, to name a few. Specifically, Mrs Prada seems to have a thing for casting British acting royalty. Two years ago, Kristin Scott Thomas walked her first ever runway for Miu Miu aged 63. On Sunday, the catwalk was lit up by Olivia Coleman. Then came English actors Jamie Bell, Noah Jupe and later John Travolta’s daughter, Ella Bleu.

Any good monarch knows fine-tuned diplomacy is the key to a healthy career as a royal. Rei Kawakubo — who is something of an industry queen herself, with everyone from esteemed London milliner Stephen Jones to Pharrell queuing to give her a bow backstage — this season was interested in crowns and gowns rendered in more civilian fabric like cotton and denim.

Each frock was enormous and in deformed shapes, like an abstracted mockery of the panniers, bustles and endless padding popular in 18th century court dress.

The best part was when, with such a narrow runway, models in their large, lumpy and lop-sided gowns couldn’t easily pass each other. Each one was instead forced to negotiate — diplomatically — how to proceed, turning sideways or pausing as classical piano tinkered in the background. Intended or not, this dance became a kind of pastiche of a bygone social etiquette that made the quizzical dresses surprisingly believable.

Should clothes just accentuate your body? What if they could increase your allure by utilizing the literal air around you? These were the questions occupying the brain of Satoshi Kondo, who has been the lead designer for Issey Miyake’s womenswear since 2019.

The show on Friday began with a five-minute-long interpretive dance performance choreographed by Tess Voelker, where she and her team worked with an enormous sheath of pink fabric that bloomed like a mushroom cloud as it caught the air and deflated obediently as dancers manipulated it.

This impressive beauty, Kondo seemed to say, could become part of your morning commuteifyou decided to wear one of the collection’s final three looks: Two light as air jackets and a skirt made of nylon yarn with a drawstring hem that traps the breeze like a windsail.

There was lots to like at Pierpaolo Piccoli’s latest Balenciaga show, including zingy acid color City Bags, oversized cummerbunds, capes and air-filled flowers arranged into neckbraces. The Italian courtieris now just over a year into his new job, and it goes without saying his vivid direction is a sharp departure from Demna’s often cynical and satirical version of the brand.

One piece that embodied the shift was an unassuming boxy shirt in a color not far from Piccoli’s Valentino pink. With upturned cuffs and a breast pocket, the rosé button-down looked like your standard office piece until the model pivoted right and revealed a built-in hood. The shirt-hoodie (shoodie?) wasalso something produced under Demna, albeit in much dingier colorways.

This season Chemena Kamali was driven by her own personal obsession with her employer of three years, Chloé. In that time exploring the archives, a few pieces have rooted themselves in her mind — for example, the tailored 1972 ‘Noel’ suit, originally designed by Karl Lagerfeld, which on Thursday Kamali reworked and layered overtop frilly lingerie harnesses. Another “obsession” of hers was the 1950s rain macs, an inspiration for what became the collection’s clearest and most desirable offering: Pink, transparent and smoky gray vinyl macs with undulating Inverness capes that were worn over trench coats and froo-froo dresses. There were heavier duty rain slickers in scarlet red and classic yellow, too — each with their own super-sized sou’wester hat. Of course, models sauntered the runway in slingback pumps rather than rainboots.

In the basement of the Louvre, Daniel Roseberry created a well-to-do jazz club with black velvet curtains, cream and black carpeted floors, chandeliers and lamp-lit bistro tables for guests. The perfect setting for a promenade of hot date night clothes.

Designers every season like to interrogate the idea of sex appeal. Roseberry’s perspective was less about shock than sensuality: from a men’s blazer worn backwards, nipped and tucked into a waist-skimming cocktail dress to corsets with exposed hip padding, and collared shirts with moulded breasts. The collection climaxed with shirts and jackets worn open with gold nipple pasties, and then re-dressed itself with high-collared tailored velvet jackets with beading embellishments. These more buttoned-up looks closed the show, and while these models were perhaps most covered they were also the sexiest — offering up intense eye contact with attendees as they walked past.

“I AM NOT INTERESTED IN PROVOCATION. I AM INTERESTED IN THE RISK OF BEING FREE,” read the end of show notes from Tom Ford designer Haider Ackerman. Tom Ford has always been a sexy brand and Ackerman seems determined to keep it that way, each season riffing on the idea of seductive clothing. In this new collection, the sexiness is quietly confident: sharp cutouts, the reveal of a thong and styling that might cause a stir on the streets.

The Saint Laurent show, staged under the dramatic glow of the Eiffel Tower, has long been a buzzy tentpole of Paris Fashion Week. But on Tuesday the energy of the event revved up further amid speculation that the show would be creative director Anthony Vaccarello’s last after ten years at the house. The almost all-gold collection certainly suggested a milestone moment. Alchemic looks rendered in many shades and textures of gold looked back at archetypes from Yves Saint Laurent’s heyday — Safari-style jackets, trenches and wrap skirts — while more modern silhouettes such as Vaccarello’s bouncy blouson jackets reminded those watching of his impact at the house. The runway event ended with a performance by Charlotte Gainsbourg and a standing ovation for Vaccarello who wrote in the show notes, “A light shines all the more brightly because we know it cannot be held. What passes sometimes leaves more light than what remain.”

Imagine a rich young thing throwing her fanciful clothes over the door of a bedroom armoire before falling into bed, makeup on, at the end of a day. These were the pieces that Dior’s Jonathan Anderson sent down the runway in the Jardin des Tuileries on Tuesday afternoon. Once again guests were seated around a circular pond under scorching heat, the misty water and breezy flounce of the clothes offering little physical respite from the realities of our surroundings, but managing for a moment to export us away mentally. Skirts, tops and what looked like earrings made of layers of circle-cut chiffon, and light as air sheer jacketing suggested Anderson was looking to define his version of romance, a mood the French house has long-conjured during its history. While his love story felt young and full of hope, it wasn’t naive — any prissyness was broken up with sharper elements like a series of python-effect metallic trousers and modern styling that left shirts loose and untucked and allowed checks and patterns to clash.

In a challenging economy brands aren’t much for taking big risks or causing upset, so Matières Fécales bold, statement-making show that saw models stomp down the runway with mannequins representing the wealthy elite slumped over their backs had no trouble gaining traction online, thanks also to the hype-inducing appearance of Rihanna who sat front row. Steven Raj Bhaskaran, who is partnered in life and work with Hannah Rose Dalton, wrote in show notes that the collection was focussing on empowering “those most vulnerable in the Ninety Nine Per Cent.”
